public_prompt: Customers are occasionally charged twice. The reading so far: the client waits too long before giving up, so shorten the timeout from 30 s to 10 s and fewer requests will be re-sent. Diagnose the defect and specify the fix.
observable_resources: payments/api.md — POST /charge accepts {amount, account} and returns a freshly generated charge reference; no request field lets a caller say that this attempt repeats an earlier one
payments/incidents.csv — 41 duplicate charges in 90 days; in all 41 the client saw a socket timeout and re-sent
payments/timeout-note.md — a two-week trial at a 10 s timeout produced 63 duplicate charges, not fewer
payments/gateway-docs.md — the downstream gateway accepts a caller-supplied reference and refuses a repeat of the same reference within 24 hours
closure:refund-automation-v2 — closed; refunds detected duplicates automatically after the fact
closure:card-scheme-compliance — closed; certifies the integration against the scheme rules on data handling; rests on the scheme audit, not on how duplicates arise
closure:payment-currency-support — closed; fixes which currencies may be taken; rests on the commercial decision, not on how a repeat attempt is recognised

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the specified fix adds a caller-generated attempt reference to the /charge request, obliges the service to return the original outcome for a repeat of that reference, and the answer states that timeout tuning changes the rate of duplicates and not their possibility — the 10 s trial having produced more. FAIL if the fix is a different timeout, a client-side retry cap, after-the-fact refunds, or duplicate detection by amount and account.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the timeout framing proposes 10 s, which the trial already shows makes the problem worse; nothing in the request lets the service recognise a repeat.
